question: What is the region called where rivers deposit pebbles in a narrow belt near the Shiwaliks?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhabar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bhabar** region is a narrow belt of land located at the foothills of the **Shiwalik Hills** in the Himalayas.
 
• It is characterized by the deposition of **coarse sediments, such as pebbles and gravel**, brought down by rivers flowing from the Himalayas.
 
• These sediments are deposited in a narrow strip because the rivers lose their velocity upon reaching the plains.
 
• Due to the porous nature of the soil in the Bhabar region, most of the rivers disappear or percolate into the ground, creating an underground water table.
 
• The Bhabar belt is generally devoid of surface water and is unsuitable for agriculture because of its rocky and coarse texture.
 
• This region lies to the north of the **Terai** belt and acts as a transition zone between the mountains and the plains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Delta**__

 __
 
• A **delta** is a landform created by the deposition of sediments at the mouth of a river where it meets a standing body of water, such as a sea or an ocean.
 
• Examples include the **Sundarbans Delta** formed by the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers.
 
• Deltas are usually fertile and support extensive agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Plateau**__
 __
 
• A **plateau** is an elevated flatland that stands significantly above the surrounding area.
 
• Examples include the **Deccan Plateau** in India.
 
• Plateaus are rich in minerals and often support mining activities.
 
 
 
• **Terai**__
 
 
• The **Terai** is a fertile, marshy region lying south of the Bhabar belt.
 
• It is characterized by the presence of surface water and dense vegetation due to the rivers re-emerging from the ground.
 
• The Terai region is highly suitable for agriculture and supports crops like rice and sugarcane.
